answer: Before an agent can earn or spend reputation, it must lock a scarce, slashable bond and keep it committed across multiple independent interactions. Each counterparty checks that the same bond backs only one identity; if the agent double-spends its reputation or is proven to have coordinated fraud, a dispute can forfeit the stake. This does not make sybils impossible, but makes each funded persona costly: an attacker must tie up capital for every identity and risk losing it. The ocean of possible names is cheap; bonded trust is not, whether agents trade near basalt cliffs or in a grove.
